title: Transfer Fidelity Stocks and RSUs to Another Broker: Shares and Cash
summary: Move Fidelity stocks or vested RSU shares to a broker that supports Indian residents without selling, or sell and wire the cash. Steps, costs and Indian tax.
body_markdown:
You can leave Fidelity without selling. Whole shares of US-listed stocks and ETFs can be transferred to another broker as they are, and if you would rather exit your positions, you can sell on Fidelity and wire the cash out instead.


This matters most to Indians who have returned from the US and to employees whose vested RSUs sit with Fidelity. Fidelity applies restrictions by country to customers who live outside the US, and in some countries an account is limited to selling holdings and withdrawing the proceeds, with no new purchases.


This guide covers both routes, moving shares and moving cash, and what each means for your Indian tax. For the general rules on moving RSU shares between brokers, see[Can I transfer my RSUs to another broker?](https://paasa.com/blog/can-i-transfer-my-rsus-to-another-broker)


## Table of contents


- Which Fidelity account do you have?
- Moving shares from Fidelity
- Moving cash from Fidelity
- Tax and reporting after the move
- Transferring your Fidelity holdings to Paasa
- About Paasa


## Which Fidelity account do you have?


The route depends on where your shares sit, so check this first.


- **A regular Fidelity brokerage account.** This is the account you opened yourself to buy US stocks and ETFs. It transfers through ACATS (Automated Customer Account Transfer Service), the standard US system for moving brokerage assets between firms.
- **A Fidelity stock plan account (NetBenefits).** This is the account your employer set up to deliver RSU or ESPP shares. Shares in it move out through Fidelity's own transfer form rather than ACATS, as explained below.


Many people have both. If you do, treat them as two separate moves.


## Moving shares from Fidelity


A transfer of shares, also called an[in-kind transfer](https://paasa.com/blog/can-you-transfer-us-stocks-to-another-broker-without-selling) , moves the same shares from Fidelity to the new broker. Nothing is sold, so there is no capital gain in India and your holding period does not restart.


### 1. From a Fidelity brokerage account


The transfer is started by your new broker, not by Fidelity. The standard process looks like this:


- You open an account at the new broker.
- You give the new broker your Fidelity account details, statements and identification documents.
- The new broker submits the request through ACATS, which notifies Fidelity.
- Fidelity validates the request within 1 business day and delivers the assets within 3 business days.
- Your shares appear in the new account.


You do not need to call Fidelity or tell them in advance. Under[FINRA's customer account transfer rules](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/key-topics/customer-account-transfers) , the firm you are leaving has to act on a valid transfer request. A sell-only restriction stops new purchases but does not block an outgoing transfer.


### 2. From a Fidelity stock plan account


Only vested shares can move. Unvested RSUs are not yet yours, so they stay with the plan until they vest.


When ACAT is not available for a stock plan account, Fidelity Stock Plan Services moves shares out through its International Transfer Request form. If you are transferring to Paasa, you will find the form in the Paasa app, together with a guide that shows how to fill in each field, including the receiving account details.


The form comes with a few rules that decide what can move and when:


- Only whole shares can be transferred. If you move all your shares, any fractional share is sold.
- Cash cannot be sent on this form, so any cash in the account has to be moved separately.
- Only shares that have met any holding period set by your plan can be transferred.
- The trade date you enter on the form must be at least 5 business days after the day you submit it.
- Once you have signed the form, you email it to Fidelity Stock Plan Services.


After you start the transfer, send your account statements and the vesting dates and details for each holding to Paasa support at support@paasa.com. This lets Paasa track the cost and gains on each holding correctly.


### 3. What can and cannot transfer


These assets transfer in-kind from a Fidelity brokerage account:


- Whole shares of US-listed stocks
- Whole shares of US-listed ETFs
- US Treasuries and bonds
- Settled cash


These do not transfer in-kind:


- Fidelity's own mutual funds, such as Fidelity Contrafund or Fidelity 500 Index Fund, which have to be sold before or during the transfer
- Fractional shares, which are sold automatically, with the cash following separately
- Unsettled trades
- Margin positions


If you hold Fidelity's own mutual funds, the rest of your portfolio can still move in-kind. Only the positions that are sold create a taxable event.


### 4. What it costs and how long it takes


Fidelity's[commission and fee schedule](https://www.fidelity.com/trading/commissions-margin-rates) lists no fee for a transfer of assets out of the account. Validation takes 1 business day and delivery takes 3 business days, so an ACATS transfer from a Fidelity brokerage account typically completes in 3 to 5 business days.


Residual amounts, such as pending dividends or proceeds from funds that had to be sold, can arrive up to 30 days after the main transfer settles. Your Fidelity account is frozen while the transfer is in progress, so you cannot trade or withdraw cash until it completes.


## Moving cash from Fidelity


The other route is to sell your shares on Fidelity and move the US dollars. This is the simpler choice when you were going to sell anyway, for example to reduce a large position in your employer's stock.


To send the proceeds to Paasa, the steps in the app are:


- **Step 1:** Download the Paasa app and complete your KYC to open your account, if you have not already.
- **Step 2:** Open the app and tap "Transfer investments".
- **Step 3:** Select Fidelity as your broker.
- **Step 4:** Select "Transfer cash".
- **Step 5:** Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the transfer.


On Fidelity's side, the stock plan[help page on wires and checks](https://nb.fidelity.com/static/sps/shtml/learn_wire_check.shtml) lists a wire to a bank and a wire to a financial institution among the ways to send money out. Fidelity says it charges USD 10 per wire, takes up to four business days to review new instructions, and generally issues the wire within five to seven business days of your request.


Online requests are limited to USD 100,000 a day, and larger amounts need a call to Fidelity Stock Plan Services. Always check the account details Paasa provides before you submit the wire.


Selling is a taxable event, unlike a transfer of shares. Once the cash is sitting abroad, the[FEMA 180-day rule](https://paasa.com/blog/fema-180-day-rule) also applies, so the proceeds have to be reinvested or brought back to India within 180 days.


## Tax and reporting after the move


A transfer of shares between two accounts that both belong to you is not a sale. You own the same shares before and after, so there is no capital gain to report and nothing to pay in India because of the move.


Your cost and holding period carry over. For RSU shares, the cost is the rupee value that was taxed as salary when the shares vested, and the holding period runs from the vesting date. The transfer changes neither, so shares held for more than 24 months from the vesting date still give a long-term gain.[Capital gains tax on RSU shares](https://paasa.com/blog/capital-gains-tax-rsu-shares) explains how the gain is worked out when you do sell.


Download a full cost basis report and your statements from Fidelity before you start. You will need the original dates and US dollar values for your Indian return, whichever broker holds the shares later.


Schedule FA still applies. If you are resident and ordinarily resident, you report the shares and the foreign account they are held in for every calendar year in which you held them. In the year of the move, you held both the Fidelity account and the new account during the calendar year, so both are reported. See[Schedule FA for RSU holders](https://paasa.com/blog/schedule-fa-rsu-holders) for the tables and values.


The transfer does not touch your LRS limit either. The shares are already abroad, so there is no rupee conversion and no fresh remittance from India.


## Transferring your Fidelity holdings to Paasa


Your Paasa account is held in your own name with Interactive Brokers as custodian, and holdings in a Fidelity brokerage account can be transferred to it directly through ACATS. Step-by-step instructions for Fidelity are in the Paasa app. Complete your sign-up, open the transfer guide for Fidelity and upload the details it asks for.


Paasa then raises the request, so you do not need to contact Fidelity. If your shares are in a stock plan account, the app gives you the International Transfer Request form and the guide to filling it in, and you send the signed form to Fidelity Stock Plan Services yourself.


For a brokerage account, Paasa supports full transfers from Fidelity, not partial ones. Fidelity's own mutual funds, fractional shares and unsettled trades need to be dealt with before the request goes in, and the team can help you plan that during onboarding. Your name on the Fidelity account has to match your name on the Paasa account exactly, or the request will be rejected.


If you need help at any point, write to support@paasa.com or message your relationship manager in the app.


## About Paasa


[Paasa](https://paasa.com/rsu) is a global investing platform built for Indian and Asian investors, giving you direct access to stocks and ETFs across the US, UK, Europe and Asia from one account.


- **Move shares without selling:** Transfer directly from Fidelity, Morgan Stanley or Schwab through an ACATS transfer, typically in 3 to 5 business days, with guidance for your specific broker.
- **Diversify once the shares arrive:** Invest in markets across 11 countries, including European-domiciled UCITS ETFs that are estate-tax safe for Indian residents.
- **Tax reports built for your ITR:** Year-end reports aligned with Indian ITR requirements, including Schedule CG and Schedule FA, are sent automatically and can be shared with your CA.
